claims.text: In the BEA '2020 Personal Income and Outlays — Historical Comparisons' table, under the 'Current dollars' section, annual PCE in 2020 declined from the preceding year by $399.3 billion (dollar change), or -2.7 percent.

citations.quotation:
2020 Personal Income and Outlays
	Historical Comparisons
Dollar change from preceding year (in billions): ... Personal consumption expenditures (PCE)	-399.3
Percent change from preceding year: ... PCE	-2.7

claims.text: Under the 'Chained dollars' section of the same annual (2020) table, PCE declined from the preceding year by $514.6 billion (dollar change), or -3.9 percent.

citations.quotation:
Chained dollars
Dollar change from preceding year (in billions): ... PCE	-514.6
Percent change from preceding year: ... PCE	-3.9

claims.text: The 2020 personal saving rate was 16.3 percent of DPI, per the 'Personal saving as a percentage of DPI' section of the annual table.

citations.quotation:
Personal saving as a percentage of DPI
Personal saving rate	16.3

claims.text: The two PCE series do not use the same basis: the first is in current dollars (nominal) and the second is in chained dollars (inflation-adjusted, real), as indicated by the separate section headings 'Current dollars' and 'Chained dollars' in the 2020 annual comparisons table.

citations.quotation:
2020 Personal Income and Outlays
	Historical Comparisons ... Current dollars

counterarguments.text: A reader might conflate this annual table with the monthly (February 2021) table in the same document, which shows a PCE monthly dollar change of -149.0 billion current dollars and -162.7 billion chained dollars; those figures refer to the change from the preceding month (February 2021), not the annual 2020 change.

citations.quotation: February 2021 Personal Income and Outlays ... Personal consumption expenditures (PCE)	-149.0

counterarguments.text: One might question whether -2.7% (current dollars) vs -3.9% (chained dollars) is consistent; it is, because the chained-dollar decline exceeds the nominal decline when prices rose (PCE price index +1.2 percent from the preceding year), but the source does not explicitly reconcile the two series.

limitations: The source is a compressed PDF table; column alignment is inferred, and some values (e.g., historical comparison periods like '1987', '1938') appear interleaved with figures, so exact column mapping for those reference periods is not fully verifiable.
The document states a publication date of March 26, 2021 and periods 2020/2019 as declared in the table; these dates are taken as stated, not independently verified.
The source does not provide the underlying 2020 and 2019 PCE levels, only year-over-year changes, so no independent recomputation of levels is possible from the text.
The chained-dollar reference year / price basis is not stated in the excerpted text.
